title: Stop Polishing: What Clients Trust in a Business Account
summary: Authentic content vs polished: what clients trust in a business account, 7 behind-the-scenes content ideas for service businesses, and human DMs.
body_markdown:
**Picture someone choosing a lash artist. Two profiles. The first is a grid of flawless, almost identical photos. The second has a shaky video of the artist laughing at a client's joke, a "before" that looks like a real Tuesday, and an "after" in normal daylight. They book the second one. Polished stopped meaning trustworthy.**


This is not a mood. Instagram's own head now says the perfect feed is over, people are tired of content that looks generated, and clients of service businesses decide where to book by looking at the people behind the account. Authentic, lo-fi content now earns more trust than polished posts. Below: what changed, what your clients look for, how authentic content differs from sloppy content, seven behind-the-scenes content ideas to post instead, and why the most real part of your account is the one nobody sees: your DMs.


## Why the perfect feed stopped working


Three things happened at once.


**People got tired of screens.** Going "analogue" turned into a trend of its own, with people swapping phones for film cameras and paper notebooks.[Dazed](https://www.dazeddigital.com/life-culture/article/69449/1/is-2026-the-year-of-analogue-tiktok-trend-social-media-offline) quotes UK regulator Ofcom: young adults spend 6 hours 20 minutes a day on screens, and only 29% of adults feel being online is good for their mental health. Social media itself is losing trust: in Sprout Social's 2026 survey, 35% of users said they trust it less than a year ago ([Sprout Social](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/building-trust-through-social-media/) ). People scroll less patiently, and they skip what looks like an ad.


**AI made "perfect" cheap.** When any business can generate a spotless photo in seconds, a spotless photo proves nothing. People notice: 78% trust videos with real people, and 36% say AI-generated content makes them lose trust in a brand ([Animoto, State of Video 2026](https://animoto.com/state-of-video) , via[Clutch](https://clutch.co/resources/unscripted-brand-content) ). Adam Mosseri, head of Instagram, put it bluntly in his year-end memo ([full text at om.co](https://om.co/2026/01/01/what-is-instagrams-adam-mosseri-really-saying-in-his-year-end-memo/) ):


> "That feed is dead. People stopped sharing personal moments to feed years ago." "Flattering imagery is cheap to produce and boring to consume. People want content that feels real. In a world where everything can be perfected, imperfection becomes a signal."


**People started craving people.** Argentine agencies interviewed by[La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/economia/negocios/el-factor-humano-cuando-mostrar-imperfecciones-se-vuelve-un-valor-de-marca-nid20092025) call it a "human craving": after the hundredth AI clip, what stands out is "not the perfect, but the imperfect: the trace, the clumsiness, the nervous laugh." Small brands there are growing with "a day in the workshop" videos that show the process, the mistakes and even the tiredness.


## What your clients look for before they book


For a service business, the account is a shop window and a first meeting at the same time. Here is what the people deciding whether to book are actually checking.


What clients check What it tells them Source


Your recent Reels and Stories That you're active and real. 55% of Gen Z and 47% of millennials call this very or extremely important before booking[Boulevard, 2026](https://www.joinblvd.com/blog/client-survey-report-2026)


Whether you feel human 47% say a stumble, a laugh or going off-script makes brand content feel more authentic and likable[Clutch, 2026](https://clutch.co/resources/unscripted-brand-content)


Who will actually do the work 56% of consumers book with the same provider every time: they choose a person, not a logo[Square](https://squareup.com/us/en/townsquare/attract-salon-customers)


Whether you answer 38% expect a reply within two hours, and 14% within minutes[Sprout Social, 2026](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/building-trust-through-social-media/)


Notice what's missing: nobody books because the lighting was expensive.


## Authentic content vs polished content


Lo-fi content is content shot and edited simply, usually on a phone, in real light, with real people and little or no styling. It looks like something a person posted, not like an ad. Authentic content goes one step further: it shows who you are and how you work, whatever the camera.


There's a catch, and Mosseri names it himself: AI will soon fake imperfection too. "At that point we'll need to shift our focus to who says something instead of what is being said." So a blurry photo on its own isn't the answer. The people, the process and the conversation are.


The data agrees that both styles have a job. The UK agency Brainlabs[analysed 46 Meta brand lift studies across 225 campaigns](https://www.brainlabsdigital.com/meta-brand-lift-studies-objectives-creatives-results/) : lo-fi, native content with an authentic human voice moved purchase intent the most (a 6% lift against 4% on average), while polished brand creative did better at building awareness with new audiences. Polished content introduces you. Authentic content sells you. And "real" never means "sloppy":


## 7 behind-the-scenes content ideas for service businesses


None of these need a studio, a ring light or an agency. A phone and ten minutes are enough.


Format 01


Salons · studios · workshops


### A day in the studio


Film one ordinary day in short clips: opening up, the first coffee, the first client, the chaos at 2 p.m., closing. This is the "day in the workshop" format that small brands in Latin America are growing with. Clients see what it's like to walk in, before they ever do.


Format 02


Beauty · clinics · repairs


### The middle, not just the before and after


A before-and-after is a promise. The middle is proof. Show the steps in between: the consultation, the prep, the part that takes forty minutes. It answers the question every new client is afraid to ask: what actually happens, and how long does it take?


Format 03


Any team


### Meet the person who'll do it


"People trust people," as the salon software company[Phorest](https://www.phorest.com/us/blog/how-to-build-trust-and-credibility-on-social-media-as-a-medi-aesthetic-clinic/) puts it in its guide for clinics: you can have a feed full of great results and still lose clients who don't know who's behind them. Introduce each specialist in 15 seconds: name, what they love doing, one thing clients always ask them.


Format 04


Clinics · coaches · consultants


### An honest "this isn't for you"


Tell people when a service won't help them: "If you want this result, laser won't get you there. Here's what will." Phorest's guide recommends exactly this, being honest about when you wouldn't recommend a treatment. Nothing builds trust faster than a business turning down a sale.


Format 05


Everyone with a DM inbox


### Real client questions, answered on camera


Your best content ideas are already in your DMs. "Does it hurt?" "How long does it last?" "Can I come after work?" Pick the question you got most this week and answer it in one take. The client who asked feels heard, and the next hundred get the answer before they write.


Format 06


Any business


### Small mistakes, fixed on camera


The cake that cracked, the delivery that came late, the color that came out too warm and how you fixed it. Keep it light and show the fix. "When we see a mistake corrected on the fly," one agency told La Nación, "we feel there are peers, not algorithms."


Format 07


When it fits


### Trends, but only the ones that fit you


A third of consumers think brands jumping on viral trends is embarrassing, and 27% think a trend works only in its first 24 to 48 hours ([Sprout Social Index](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/press/the-days-of-trend-chasing-are-over-new-research-from-sprout-social-reveals-a-third-of-consumers-think-jumping-on-viral-trends-is-embarrassing-for-brands/) ). Take a trend only when your client can see themselves in it. We pick the ones that fit small businesses every week in[Instagram Reels Trends This Week](https://chatfuel.com/blog/instagram-reels-trends) .


## The most real part of your account is your DMs


A real feed does one job: it makes someone want to talk to you. Then they open a chat. Mosseri says the DMs are now where people share, and clients of service businesses agree: 44% prefer texting as a way to communicate with a salon or spa ([Boulevard](https://www.salontoday.com/news/boulevard-consumer-surveys-shows-gen-z-and-millennials-are-redefining-the-self-care-experience) ). And when something goes wrong, 55% of consumers would rather slide into a company's DMs than complain publicly ([Sprout Social, 2026](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/the-state-of-social-media/) ).


This is where many accounts lose everything the feed built. The Reel felt human; the reply comes two days later, or it reads like a call center.


the reply that kills it


hi! any slots this saturday? 🙏


Thank you for contacting us. Your request is important to us. Please select an option: 1. Services 2. Prices 3. Location


the reply that books


hi! any slots this saturday? 🙏


Hi! Saturday we have 11:00 and 15:30 with Anna. Lash lift is $60, about an hour. Want me to hold one for you?


The second reply doesn't need a person typing at 10:40 p.m. It needs an AI agent that knows your services, your prices and your free time, talks like you, and hands the chat to you when it should.


## Keep replies human, even when you're not the one typing


What makes an AI reply sound like your business instead of a call center:


- **Your tone.** Short messages, your words, the customer's language. Tone, greeting and reply length live in the AI's main prompt.
- **Your facts.** Services, prices, opening hours and the FAQ your clients really ask, in the Knowledge Base. The AI answers from them, not from guesses.
- **Your limits.** Always/never rules in the instructions ("never promise a result", "never discuss medical history in chat").
- **You, when it matters.** Handoff rules send complaints, refunds or anything unusual to a person. When you reply yourself, the AI steps back.
- **Your comments.** Someone comments "price?" under a Reel, gets a short public reply and the price list in DMs. The conversation starts where the interest is.

## FAQs


### What is lo-fi content on Instagram?


Lo-fi content is simple, unpolished content: shot on a phone, in natural light, with real people and little editing. On Instagram it looks like a post from a person rather than an ad, which is why it often feels more trustworthy. For a business, the best lo-fi content shows the people and the process behind the service.


### Does unpolished content work for premium services like clinics?


Yes, as long as it's real and not careless. Clinics build trust by showing the specialists, the process and honest advice about who a treatment suits, which is what Phorest's guide for aesthetic clinics recommends. Keep the before-and-after photos clear and get written consent from patients.


### How often should a small business post behind-the-scenes content?


Often enough that the account looks alive when a client checks it before booking. One or two short behind-the-scenes Reels or Stories a week is a realistic rhythm for a small team. Consistency matters more than production.


### Will clients know they're talking to an AI in my DMs?


What clients notice is whether the reply is fast, specific and sounds like you. Set a short, warm tone in the AI's main prompt, give it your real prices and hours, and add handoff rules so complaints and unusual requests go to a person.
